text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.7% today after oil prices dropped for a second day on hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict, easing near-term supply concerns that had driven crude up sharply last week. The stock had surged $7 in four days through Thursday on geopolitical tension, but that rally reversed when market sentiment shifted toward negotiation rather than escalation.

The broader headwind is political: Democrats appear set to sweep the midterm elections, and energy investors are weighing the possibility of a Congress more focused on offshore wind and solar development. For an oil producer, that translates to longer-term policy uncertainty, though today's immediate move tracks the day-to-day swings in crude itself—the price of oil is where ConocoPhillips earnings ultimately come from.
